payload.reason: Only one proposal was offered (practice). Its core is taken, but its recorder rig is dropped. Criterion 1 is built as a record line in the test output, and criteria 2 and 3 are filed for the person, as the survey's checked_by says.
payload.selection_rationale:
The survey decides what this slice has to build. Criterion 1 is checked_by loop and is missing: no file in src/, tests/ or eng/ reads Get-MpPreference, and the fsutil state that CFA must sit beside is written at HeldOpenTreeTests.cs:135, with the Fsutil helper at :342. Criteria 2 and 3 are checked_by person. Arming CFA takes an administrator, Windows Sandbox cannot run Defender at all (measured: WinDefend DISABLED, 1058, 0x800106ba), and only a person at the desktop sees a notification. So the slice builds the record and nothing that judges 2 or 3.

The practice proposal's core matches the code as it is shaped today, and it is kept:
- one record line beside the fsutil line, read by spawning a process the way the Fsutil helper does;
- the read never asserts, skips or throws;
- no xUnit Fact for CFA=on. The Microsoft-signed testhost image could be allowed by reputation, and an opt-in Fact would cost a Trait, a filter clause and a pin (#198, and #381 if it landed in LastAccessUnderSystemRootTests);
- no product change. Spike #109 already measured that a refused keep-open falls back to a full listing, and Q-159 keeps LastAccessAsked/Kept internal (#328).

Three parts of the proposal are rejected against reality:
1. tests/window/CfaScan.ps1, its canary build and its CFA-off rehearsal log. The designer raised over_engineering_flag themselves and called the recorder borderline. It is a rig that measures the problem (it finds out what CFA does), and that belongs to a spike or to the person's session, not to the slice. A new .ps1 under tests/ also lands in AppArgumentTests' launch-line census, which an untracked script already turned red once (#412). The person's steps go into the design doc as pasteable commands instead.
2. Counting the protected and allowed lists in PowerShell with Measure-Object. The child now emits raw JSON and C# counts. The @($null).Count=1 class of bug moves out of untestable script text and into a pure function that a default-suite Theory pins.
3. The helper moves out of HeldOpenTreeTests.cs into its own DefenderState.cs, so its never-throw paths (non-zero exit, timeout kill, exe missing, unparsed output) can be exercised on this PC unattended.

One robustness step the proposal lacked is added: the child gets no inherited PSModulePath. eng/dotnet.ps1 runs under pwsh 7, so testhost would otherwise hand pwsh 7's module path to Windows PowerShell 5.1.

components.name: DefenderState record helper
components.responsibility:
Produces the one 'Controlled Folder Access:' line.

The read:
- Starts %SystemRoot%\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command with $ErrorActionPreference='Stop'.
- PSModulePath is removed from the child's environment.
- The child emits one compact JSON object: enable, protected and allowed (raw values of EnableControlledFolderAccess, ControlledFolderAccessProtectedFolders and ControlledFolderAccessAllowedApplications from Get-MpPreference), and mode, rtp and platform (AMRunningMode, RealTimeProtectionEnabled and AMProductVersion from Get-MpComputerStatus).
- It waits at most 20 s, then kills the process tree.
- The result is cached in a static Lazy<string> (thread-safe), so it is read once per test process.

A pure Describe(exitCode, stdout, stderr, timedOut, startException) turns the result into the line:
- It counts a list as null→0, []→0, scalar string→1, array→length.
- It maps enable 0..4 to names and always prints the raw value.
- A missing property prints as '?'.
- Any failure becomes 'Controlled Folder Access: not read (<reason>)'.

It never asserts, skips or throws.
components.key_interactions: It is called once from HeldOpenTreeTests at the fsutil record point. Its runner takes the file name, arguments and timeout as parameters, so DefenderStateRecordTests can drive the kill and start-failure paths. It reads only (Get-* cmdlets), and an architecture rule forbids any Set/Add/Remove-MpPreference under tests/.

components.name: CFA record point in HeldOpenTreeTests
components.responsibility: Writes DefenderState.Line to the same test output, on the line after the `fsutil behavior query disablelastaccess` output (:135). That makes the CFA state recorded where the scan's last-access results are recorded, as SL-056's design asked (docs/design/SL-056-probe-every-file.md:107-108). It adds no new Fact, Trait or filter clause.
components.key_interactions: Sits beside the existing Fsutil helper (:342). FsaDefaultTestFilter, OptInTraitTests and the pinned Fact array in LastAccessRuleCorpusTests (which covers LastAccessUnderSystemRootTests, not this class) are untouched (#198, #381).

components.name: DefenderStateRecordTests
components.key_interactions: Runs in the existing Core.Tests project through eng/dotnet.ps1 (#72). It must stay compatible with CountingRuleTestsAreNeverSkipped and OptInTraitTests: no Trait, no Skip, no Explicit.

components.name: SL-101 design note and person-run recipe
components.responsibility:
Records:
- the line's format and where it appears, plus the reading taken at validate;
- the person's recipe for criteria 2 and 3, with a results table and a reading key.

The recipe, in order:
1. Read and write down the current EnableControlledFolderAccess value (unelevated).
2. Build a fixture R under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp\fsa-cfa-<hex>\R, never %TEMP% (#360).
3. Publish with eng/dotnet.ps1.
4. In an elevated shell, arm AuditMode first and then Enabled, and add R to the protected folders. The Windows Security UI is the fallback if Tamper Protection refuses the cmdlet.
5. Scan R with eng/read-window.ps1 -Root R (#84). Write down the outcome, counters, unreadable count and entry count against the fixture.
6. Watch for a notification.
7. Run a pasteable, csc-built unsigned canary that writes into R, as the positive control.
8. Count 1123/1124 events naming FsAnalyser.App.exe, canary.exe and R, unelevated, with -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue.
9. Disarm to the recorded value, and delete the fixture only once R is off the list.

The reading key ties outcomes to spike #109:
- no canary event: the run is void;
- canary event and no scanner event: not blocked;
- scanner 1123 with a full listing and 0 unreadable: blocked and fell back;
- a short listing or unreadable > 0: contradicts spike #109 and needs a defect slice.

The results are evidence for the still-open Q-101. The note does not answer it.
components.key_interactions: Cites SL-056's design note without editing it. Cites spike #109 for the refusal-to-outcome mapping. It is the material for filed_for_later items 1 and 2.

components.name: Keep-open fallback (reused, unchanged)
components.responsibility: TryOpenKeepingLastAccess returns false on any failure of the write-attributes open or of the FileBasicInfo set, and Open then does a plain open. Spike #109 measured 'go' for both the root and a subfolder: full listing, 0 unreadable, Kept 5→4.
components.key_interactions: Scanner.ListRoot, DecideLastAccess, KeepsLastAccess and CountListingOpen (Scanner.cs:222-347) and DirectoryReader.Open (:66-67, :90-99) reach it. It is the reason no product change is designed here.

components.name: Published exe report path (reused)
components.responsibility: The person scans the fixture with the real unsigned single-file exe, which is the image CFA judges in the field. The exe returns the schema-1 window and core fields.
components.key_interactions: Needs artifacts/publish/FsAnalyser.App.exe from `pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 publish src/FsAnalyser.App/FsAnalyser.App.csproj -c Release -o artifacts/publish`. Only the person's recipe uses it in this slice.

contracts.name: Controlled Folder Access record line (test output)
contracts.error_cases: Each of these prints `Controlled Folder Access: not read (<reason>)` and the test carries on exactly as before: Defender not running or a third-party AV (non-zero exit, first stderr line as the reason), Sandbox 0x800106ba, empty or non-JSON stdout ('unparsed output'), a child exceeding 20 s ('timed out after 20 s', process tree killed), and powershell.exe failing to start (the exception type and message).
contracts.notes: Format: `Controlled Folder Access: EnableControlledFolderAccess=<raw> (<Disabled|Enabled|AuditMode|BlockDiskModificationOnly|AuditDiskModificationOnly|unknown>), protected folders=<n>, allowed apps=<n>; Defender AMRunningMode=<s|?>, RealTimeProtection=<bool|?>, platform=<version|?>`. The raw value is always printed, so a wrong name mapping (recalled) cannot hide the value. It appears on the line after the DisableLastAccess output in HeldOpenTreeTests. On this PC today it should read EnableControlledFolderAccess=0 (Disabled), protected folders=0, allowed apps=1, AMRunningMode=Normal, RealTimeProtection=True.

contracts.name: DefenderState.Describe
contracts.error_cases: Total over all inputs. It never throws. Unknown enable values print the raw value with '(unknown)'.
contracts.notes: Inputs: exitCode, stdout, stderr, timedOut, startException. Output: the record line. The list counting rule is null→0, []→0, JSON string→1, array→length. Parsing uses System.Text.Json from the BCL; no package is added.

contracts.name: Defender read child process
contracts.auth_model: Ordinary user. It calls read-only Get-MpPreference and Get-MpComputerStatus, and never requests elevation.
contracts.error_cases: A terminating error (ErrorActionPreference Stop) gives a non-zero exit and stderr, which Describe turns into 'not read'.
contracts.notes: `%SystemRoot%\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command "$ErrorActionPreference='Stop'; $p=Get-MpPreference; $s=Get-MpComputerStatus; [pscustomobject]@{enable=$p.EnableControlledFolderAccess; protected=$p.ControlledFolderAccessProtectedFolders; allowed=$p.ControlledFolderAccessAllowedApplications; mode=$s.AMRunningMode; rtp=$s.RealTimeProtectionEnabled; platform=$s.AMProductVersion} | ConvertTo-Json -Compress"`. PSModulePath is removed from the child's environment, so 5.1 builds its own default module path.

contracts.name: Person-run arm and disarm commands (in the design note, run by the person)
contracts.auth_model: Administrator, in the person's own elevated shell. No engine stage and no file under tests/ runs them (architecture rule).
contracts.error_cases: Tamper Protection or policy may refuse Set-MpPreference. For Enabled, the fallback is Windows Security > Virus & threat protection > Manage ransomware protection. AuditMode has no UI switch (recalled), so if the cmdlet is refused the Audit row is recorded as skipped.
contracts.notes: Arm: `Set-MpPreference -EnableControlledFolderAccess AuditMode` (then `Enabled`) and `Add-MpPreference -ControlledFolderAccessProtectedFolders '<R>'`. Disarm: `Remove-MpPreference -ControlledFolderAccessProtectedFolders '<R>'` and `Set-MpPreference -EnableControlledFolderAccess <value recorded before arming>`.

cases.behaviour: record the CFA state beside the fsutil state
cases.shape: CFA is off on a PC where Defender is running (this PC: EnableControlledFolderAccess=0)
cases.why: This is criterion 1 itself. The line has to exist, sit on the line after the DisableLastAccess output, and carry the value a fresh read gives.
cases.check: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 test tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests --filter "FullyQualifiedName~HeldOpenTree" --logger "console;verbosity=detailed" → exit 0, and the output line after the 'DisableLastAccess' line starts 'Controlled Folder Access: EnableControlledFolderAccess=<n>', where <n> equals `powershell.exe -NoProfile -Command "(Get-MpPreference).EnableControlledFolderAccess"` (0 today)

cases.behaviour: record the CFA state beside the fsutil state
cases.shape: testhost was launched from pwsh 7 (eng/dotnet.ps1), so it inherits pwsh 7's PSModulePath
cases.why: Windows PowerShell 5.1 started with pwsh 7's module path can load the wrong modules or fail to load the Defender module. The PSModulePath removal exists for exactly this case.
cases.check: The same eng/dotnet.ps1 HeldOpenTree run under pwsh, as above: the Controlled Folder Access line is not 'not read (...)'

cases.shape: the list is empty and serialises as JSON null
cases.why: In PowerShell an empty list counted naively reads as 1 (@($null).Count). Today's PC has an empty list and must read 'protected folders=0'.
cases.check: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 test tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests --filter "FullyQualifiedName~DefenderStateRecordTests" → the null-list row passes (count 0)

cases.behaviour: count the protected-folder or allowed-apps list
cases.shape: the list arrives as a single JSON string, not an array
cases.why: How Windows PowerShell 5.1's ConvertTo-Json renders a one-element string[] property is recalled, not measured. A scalar must count as 1, not as its character length.
cases.check: eng/dotnet.ps1 test ... --filter "FullyQualifiedName~DefenderStateRecordTests" → the scalar row passes (count 1)

cases.behaviour: count the protected-folder or allowed-apps list
cases.shape: the list is an array of several entries
cases.why: This is the shape after the person adds R to the protected list. The count must equal the array length.
cases.check: eng/dotnet.ps1 test ... --filter "FullyQualifiedName~DefenderStateRecordTests" → the two-element row passes (count 2)

cases.why: The person's recommended first run is AuditMode, so the line must name it and still print the raw 2.
cases.check: eng/dotnet.ps1 test ... --filter "FullyQualifiedName~DefenderStateRecordTests" → the enable-2 row yields 'EnableControlledFolderAccess=2 (AuditMode)'

cases.shape: the enable value is a number outside 0..4
cases.why: The name mapping is recalled, and a future Defender may add values. The unknown branch must print the raw number rather than throw or misname it.
cases.check: eng/dotnet.ps1 test ... --filter "FullyQualifiedName~DefenderStateRecordTests" → the enable-7 row yields 'EnableControlledFolderAccess=7 (unknown)'

cases.shape: a property (AMRunningMode, AMProductVersion) is missing from the JSON
cases.why: Older Defender platforms, such as an unmeasured Windows 10 one, may lack a property. The line must print '?' instead of failing.
cases.check: eng/dotnet.ps1 test ... --filter "FullyQualifiedName~DefenderStateRecordTests" → the missing-property row prints 'AMRunningMode=?'

cases.behaviour: record the CFA state without failing the test
cases.shape: the child exits non-zero with stderr (Defender not running, Sandbox 0x800106ba, third-party AV)
cases.why: Counting-rule tests are never skipped. If the read failure leaked out, every HeldOpenTree Fact on a machine without Defender would go red for a reason unrelated to counting.
cases.check: eng/dotnet.ps1 test ... --filter "FullyQualifiedName~DefenderStateRecordTests" → the non-zero-exit row yields 'not read (<first stderr line>)' and does not throw

cases.behaviour: record the CFA state without failing the test
cases.shape: stdout is empty or is not JSON
cases.why: A profile banner, a warning or a partial write would otherwise throw from the JSON parser inside a counting-rule test.
cases.check: eng/dotnet.ps1 test ... --filter "FullyQualifiedName~DefenderStateRecordTests" → the empty-stdout and non-JSON rows yield 'not read (unparsed output)'

cases.behaviour: record the CFA state without failing the test
cases.shape: the child runs past the timeout
cases.why: A hung powershell.exe would hang HeldOpenTree and the engine's suite. The kill path must return promptly and leave no child behind.
cases.check: eng/dotnet.ps1 test ... --filter "FullyQualifiedName~DefenderStateRecordTests" → the timeout Fact (1 s timeout, child runs Start-Sleep 5) returns 'not read (timed out after 1 s)' in under 10 s

cases.behaviour: record the CFA state without failing the test
cases.shape: the executable cannot be started (file does not exist)
cases.why: Process.Start throws Win32Exception. That throw must become 'not read' rather than escape.
cases.check: eng/dotnet.ps1 test ... --filter "FullyQualifiedName~DefenderStateRecordTests" → the missing-exe Fact returns a line starting 'Controlled Folder Access: not read ('

cases.behaviour: record the CFA state once per test process
cases.shape: several HeldOpenTree Facts ask for the line in one process, possibly in parallel
cases.why: Lazy<string> in its default thread-safe mode only saves a second 1-2 s spawn. An uncached or racing read would still print a correct line, so this is speed, not correctness.
cases.check: not owed: judged not worth a test (performance only)

cases.behaviour: keep the default suite's opt-in machinery intact
cases.shape: a new test class (DefenderStateRecordTests) joins Core.Tests
cases.why: Under #198, a stray Trait, Skip or Explicit on the new class would break the never-skipped guard or the opt-in filter pin.
cases.check: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 test tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests --filter "FullyQualifiedName~OptInTraitTests|FullyQualifiedName~NeverSkipped" → exit 0

architecture_rules.name: no test or test script changes Microsoft Defender's settings
architecture_rules.because: Arming or disarming Controlled Folder Access needs an administrator, and the project never asks for admin rights. A test that did it would fail in every ordinary run, and in an elevated run it would silently change the machine's ransomware protection for every app. The person does it by hand from docs/design/SL-101-controlled-folder-access.md, which is outside this glob. The survey's grep found no MpPreference anywhere in tests/ at 9851b9c, so the rule starts clean.

key_decisions.decision: Criterion 1 is met by a test-output record: one 'Controlled Folder Access:' line written by HeldOpenTreeTests on the line after the fsutil DisableLastAccess output. No product code in Core or App reads Defender state.
key_decisions.rationale: That is where the survey measured the last-access state being recorded (HeldOpenTreeTests.cs:135), and it is what SL-056's note asked for. Putting a Defender read in the product would be a feature that Q-159 (counters internal, no message to the person) never asked for.

key_decisions.decision: The state is read by spawning Windows PowerShell 5.1 (full System32 path, PSModulePath removed from the child) running Get-MpPreference and Get-MpComputerStatus, which emit raw JSON. Lists are counted in C#.
key_decisions.rationale: Get-MpPreference is the only route measured working unelevated on this PC. The HKLM Exploit Guard value is unmeasured for ordinary users and misses policy-set state, and WMI through System.Management would add a package. Counting in C# moves the @($null).Count pitfall out of script text and into a pure function a Theory pins. The PSModulePath strip protects against the pwsh 7 parent that eng/dotnet.ps1 always provides.

key_decisions.decision: The record never asserts, skips or throws. Every failure is 'not read (<reason>)', with a 20 s timeout and kill, cached once per process.
key_decisions.rationale: A machine's Defender setting is not a test outcome, and counting-rule tests may not be skipped. On machines without Defender the line says 'not read' and nothing turns red.

key_decisions.decision: No xUnit Fact, Trait or filter clause exercises CFA=on.
key_decisions.rationale: testhost.exe and dotnet.exe are Microsoft-signed and may be allowed by CFA's trust check (recalled), so such a Fact could measure the wrong image and report 'not blocked'. An opt-in Fact would also cost a Trait, a FsaDefaultTestFilter clause and an OptInTraitTests pin (#198), and LastAccessUnderSystemRootTests forbids Traits (#381). Arming CFA also needs an administrator, which no engine stage has.

key_decisions.decision: Criteria 2 and 3 are filed for the person. The slice ships no recorder script, no canary build and no CFA-off rehearsal log, only a pasteable recipe and results table in the design note.
key_decisions.rationale: The survey marks both as checked_by person. The practice designer flagged their own recorder as borderline over-engineering, and a rig that measures CFA belongs to a spike or to the person's session, not to the slice (every review would attack its edge cases). A new tests/*.ps1 would also join AppArgumentTests' launch-line census, which an untracked script already broke once (#412). The cost is that the person's steps have not been executed before they run them (cf. Q-235, #340), and the recipe says so.

key_decisions.decision: The CFA=on outcome is observed from outside: the published exe's schema-1 report, the Defender 1123/1124 log and the person's eyes. LastAccessAsked/Kept stay internal and no report field is added.
key_decisions.rationale: Q-159 (answered) keeps the counters internal, and #328 warns that internal counters are not the public shape. Spike #109 already maps a refusal to 'full listing, asked but not kept', so a 1123 naming the exe plus a full listing settles the outcome without exposing the counter. Making the counters public is the expensive change this avoids.

key_decisions.decision: No product change and no KnownWorkarounds entry in this slice.
key_decisions.rationale: No defect outside the project is established. CFA refusing an untrusted app's write-attributes open may be Defender working as intended, and spike #109 shows the scanner degrades to a full listing if it does. If the person's run shows a 1123 block or a notification caused by the scan, a follow-up slice decides the behaviour. That includes whether skipping the keep-open in protected folders is a workaround entry under the one-checkbox-per-bug rule, and whether Q-159 reopens.

key_decisions.decision: The person's fixture is a custom protected folder under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp\fsa-cfa-<hex>\R. AuditMode is armed before Enabled, an unsigned canary write is the positive control, and the person disarms to the value recorded before arming.
key_decisions.rationale: This avoids scanning personal data. %TEMP% is hostile in engine shells (#360). A OneDrive-redirected Documents is never asked to keep (Scanner.cs:296-306), so a run there would read 'not blocked' for the wrong reason. Audit-first is Microsoft's recommendation (cited). Without the canary, 0 scanner events cannot be told from 'CFA never armed on R'.

proposals.note: Kept: the record line beside the fsutil line, the never-throw read through spawned Windows PowerShell, no CFA Fact, no product change, observation from outside, criteria 2 and 3 filed for the person, %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp fixture, audit-first and canary in the person recipe. Cut: tests/window/CfaScan.ps1, the canary build, the JSONL run log and the CFA-off rehearsal (the designer's own over_engineering_flag, and a measuring rig in a slice). Changed: the helper gets its own file with a unit-tested pure Describe, counting moves from Measure-Object to C# over raw JSON, and PSModulePath is stripped from the child.

payload.coherence_check:
One proposal, so there is no composition to check. Nothing in this design has yet survived a disagreement, and the reviewer downstream is the first to argue with it.

Seams checked inside the single proposal and the changes made to it:
1. Never-throw against the timeout kill. The kill path and Process.Start failures both route through Describe, and the timeout and missing-exe Facts pin them.
2. Lazy caching against xUnit class parallelism. Lazy<string>'s default mode is thread-safe, so two classes asking at once still spawn one child.
3. Never-skipped policy against a machine-state read. The read never asserts or skips; 'not read' is a valid line.
4. Opt-in machinery. The new class has no Trait or Skip, and LastAccessUnderSystemRootTests' pinned Fact array is untouched (#381).
5. AppArgumentTests' .ps1 launch census. Dropping CfaScan.ps1 means no new script, which removes the #412 risk.
6. The person recipe against the single architecture rule. The recipe's Set/Add/Remove-MpPreference commands live in docs/, outside the tests/** glob, so the rule and the recipe do not contradict.

The one rule is engine-appended as a settled rule, not twinned. SL-069's derived-baseline counts mean RuleCases' settled count should absorb it, and validate should still run C-001.

No decidable disagreements are recorded. The only open empirical question is whether the 5.1 child reads Defender inside the engine's testhost, and the loser of that changes only the helper's internals (the 'not read' line), not any contract.

Validate should run the whole Core.Tests default suite. The three Q-190 last-access failures under TEMP=C:\WINDOWS\TEMP predate this slice (#353).
taste_disagreements: Recorder script against doc recipe: the proposal shipped tests/window/CfaScan.ps1 (-Prepare/-Observe/-Cleanup, JSONL, canary build, CFA-off rehearsal under both shells) so the person runs rehearsed code. The composition ships pasteable steps in the design note instead, trading rehearsal for less review surface and no AppArgumentTests exposure.

Helper placement: the proposal put the read beside the Fsutil helper inside HeldOpenTreeTests.cs. The composition gives it its own DefenderState.cs so its never-throw and counting shapes can be unit-tested.
Where the lists are counted: the proposal used Measure-Object in PowerShell. The composition emits raw JSON and counts in C#.

Positive control in the person recipe: an unsigned csc canary (chosen) against pointing the exe's own --report into R, which would use the same image but whose behaviour when the write is refused is unknown.
Rule scope: the Defender-settings rule covers tests/** only. eng/** and src/** could be added as separate entries if a later reviewer judges them likely places for such a call.

filed_for_later.what:
Criterion 2: on this PC, as administrator, follow docs/design/SL-101-controlled-folder-access.md:
1. Record the current EnableControlledFolderAccess value.
2. Build R under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp\fsa-cfa-<hex>.
3. Publish the exe.
4. Arm AuditMode and add R to the protected folders. Scan R with eng/read-window.ps1 -Root R. Run the unsigned canary into R.
5. Repeat with Enabled.
6. Disarm to the recorded value and delete the fixture.

Fill in the results table: CFA mode seen, R protected, outcome and counters, unreadable count, entries listed against the fixture, canary exit and event. Read it with the spike #109 key. An optional Documents run is meaningful only if Documents is not under a OneDrive root. The results are evidence for Q-101, which stays open until they exist.
filed_for_later.why: Arming CFA changes a machine-wide Defender security setting and takes an administrator. Windows Sandbox cannot host the run: Defender is disabled there (measured: WinDefend DISABLED, 1058, error 5 as SYSTEM, 0x800106ba). The survey marks this criterion checked_by person.

filed_for_later.what: Criterion 3: during each armed scan, note whether a Windows Security notification appeared. Afterwards, count Defender Operational events 1123 and 1124 whose message names FsAnalyser.App.exe and a path under R; this read needs no elevation. Record both in the results table.
filed_for_later.why: A toast can only be seen by a person at the desktop. The events exist only after a person has armed CFA as administrator. The survey marks this criterion checked_by person.

filed_for_later.what: If the person's run shows a 1123 block naming FsAnalyser.App.exe, a CFA notification caused by the scan, or a short listing or unreadable > 0: decide the product behaviour. Options include skipping the keep-last-access open in CFA-protected folders and judging whether that is a KnownWorkarounds entry (one checkbox, on by default, with the in-app notice). Reopen Q-159 if a notification is user-visible.
filed_for_later.why: It depends on evidence only the person's run produces, and it is a product change to the scanner. This slice changes no product code.

filed_for_later.what: Exercise the TryOpenKeepingLastAccess branch where the FILE_WRITE_ATTRIBUTES open succeeds but SetFileInformationByHandle(FileBasicInfo) fails. CFA might take this branch, spike #109 did not exercise it, and the fallback there rests on reading SynchronousIoCancel.cs:529-543.
filed_for_later.why: An ACL cannot produce 'open OK, set refused'. It needs an injection seam in Core's open path, which does not exist (SL-082: DirectoryReader is hardcoded and not injectable). That is scanner work above this slice's scope.

filed_for_later.what: Repeat the criterion 2/3 run on a Windows 10 machine and on a later Defender platform than 4.18.26080.4.
filed_for_later.why: No Windows 10 machine exists here (Q-205, Q-224), and CFA's interception can change between Defender platform updates. Only a person can supply the machine.

outside_claims.claim: Get-MpPreference and Get-MpComputerStatus return EnableControlledFolderAccess, the protected-folder and allowed-app lists, AMRunningMode and RealTimeProtectionEnabled to a non-elevated user on this PC.
outside_claims.source: survey: non-elevated read (elevated=False) gave EnableControlledFolderAccess=0, empty protected list, 1 allowed app, AMRunningMode=Normal, RTP on
outside_claims.if_wrong: The line would read 'not read' everywhere and criterion 1 would not be met. The route would need to change to the registry or WMI (helper internals only).

outside_claims.claim: Windows PowerShell 5.1 is present at %SystemRoot%\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe on Windows 10 and 11 and carries the Defender cmdlets (ConfigDefender module).
outside_claims.source: memory; powershell.exe is already spawned by RuleCopiesAgreeTests (Q-028), but the Defender module under 5.1 specifically was not measured
outside_claims.if_wrong: The line reads 'not read' (the start-failure or non-zero-exit path) and criterion 1 is unmet until the route changes.

cross_domain_transfer.source_domain: Endpoint-security rollout (Microsoft Defender Controlled Folder Access / ASR evaluation in organisations). Selected in part: it shapes only the person-run recipe in the design note, not shipped code.
cross_domain_transfer.pattern: Run the rule in audit mode first, then enabled. Prove it is armed with a deliberately untrusted test app writing into the protected folder (a positive control). Judge the app under test by the Defender event log (1123 blocked, 1124 audited) rather than by the app's own view of itself.
cross_domain_transfer.rationale: Those are exactly the failure modes that would make a single person-run worthless: a mistyped or unapplied protected path reading as 'not blocked', a Microsoft-signed host that reputation allows reading as 'not blocked', and a notification nobody connects to a cause. The canary covers the first, scanning with the published unsigned exe covers the second, and the event log covers the third. Observing through the event log also keeps LastAccessAsked/Kept internal (Q-159, #328).

prior_art.pattern: Run CFA in audit mode first, then enabled, and measure its effect from CFA events rather than alerts (CFA blocks don't raise Alerts-queue items).
Use a deliberately unsigned, untrusted test app writing a file into a protected folder to see CFA evaluate and block it. This is the positive-control idea behind the recipe's canary.
The CFA test tool needs Defender enabled and in active mode, which is why the Sandbox, with Defender disabled, cannot host the run.
View and change protected folders through Windows Security > Ransomware protection > Manage ransomware protection, and search CFA events in Event Viewer. This is the UI fallback in the recipe.

Detect CFA from the registry value EnableControlledFolderAccess under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\Controlled Folder Access. Rejected in favour of the measured unelevated Get-MpPreference.
CFA decides by app trust (signature and cloud reputation). Microsoft-signed binaries are generally allowed, and freshly built unsigned exes are the classic false-positive victims.
prior_art.where: Microsoft Defender CFA documentation and community reports

prior_art.pattern: Event IDs 1123 (blocked) and 1124 (audited) are in Microsoft-Windows-Windows Defender/Operational. Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable throws 'No events were found' on an empty result.
prior_art.where: Microsoft Defender event reference; PowerShell Get-WinEvent behaviour

prior_art.pattern: Tamper Protection can refuse Defender preference changes made by cmdlet even from an elevated shell, so a UI path is needed as a fallback.
In PowerShell, @($null).Count is 1, so an empty preference list miscounts if counted naively. This is the reason counting moved to C# over raw JSON.
